text:
Easton Cowan's rookie year brought 29 points in 66 games. Nineteen games into his second, he has 14 points and six goals, and on Nov. 2 the Leafs put him back on Auston Matthews' line, per TSN and Toronto Hockey Daily. He's playing 15.7 minutes a night, and The Hockey News' Mike Fink singled him out as a London Knights alum stepping up for Toronto.

Some of it is running hot. He's shooting 16.2% against a talent range near 13%, and Toronto has scored 4.5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on. Our projection settles at about 50 points. He has also gone four games without a point as the Leafs lost three straight.

The encouraging part is how he creates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for primary shot assists, with 60% of his shots coming off the rush (a nine-game sample). His name has surfaced in trade talk too: Yardbarker floated that a Leafs blockbuster may have to include him. For a 28th overall pick at 21, that says plenty about his value.
headline: Cowan's second season, back beside Matthews
